articles.summary: Dark indigo satin with faint tonal blisters and contour rings, subtle sparkle, reads almost flat black at distance. A dark indigo-purple field with a busy swirled ripple texture and yellow and cyan hairlines; reads moody, techy and finely patterned.
articles.what: Eccentric contour orders surrounding displaced skin blisters. Colored inspection artwork with bulge contours, order shoulders, disbond rims, phase discontinuities, isolat Up close: Dark navy ground crowded with overlapping concentric ellipse rings in magenta-purple, 40-120 px across, like interferogram fringe maps; thin yellow outline loops, short cyan crack ticks and tiny bright pinpoints at ring centres. Rings overlap heavily so dense tangled spirals form. From a distance: A dark indigo-purple field with a busy swirled ripple texture and yellow and cyan hairlines; reads moody, techy and finely patterned. Measured spec (average): metal 98, roughness 61, coat 138. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, roof.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Holographic Interferogram" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, trunk: wide panels show whole rings
Doors and quarters: dense tangle fills well without a clear focal point
White or bright yellow numbers read well; dark or purple numbers vanish.
Large bold shapes or stripes in light colours: strong contrast reads over the dark rings
Pairs well with: matte black, chrome trim, deep purple, silver.
pitfalls: Not a hologram foil: no rainbow colour sweep, rings are purple-magenta with yellow accents
Not marble or swirl paint: rings are crisp concentric ellipses
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, small numbers.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 98 (pearl-level metal), roughness 61 (satin gloss), clearcoat 138 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, small numbers.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold shapes or stripes in light colours: strong contrast reads over the dark rings; big soft panel fades: the ring texture continues under them
Patterns to avoid: fine geometry, hex or topographic line patterns: compete with the rings; dense camo or noise: clutter on already busy texture
Spec overlays that work: broad gloss clearcoat: sharpens the ring glints on a dark base; coarse metallic flake: adds sparkle in the open navy areas
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Isoclinic Band
articles.summary: Dark satin surface crossed by four-lobed bowtie bands of light and shadow, like stretched fabric or a stress map. Reads as a pattern of dark swirls and pinwheels on a lighter colour, like twisted fabric or a bent marble pattern; contrast is strong and survives from far away.
articles.what: the dark loci where a principal stress axis lines up with the polariser Up close: Light mid-tone field with sweeping dark curved bands that pinch together into pinwheel nodes, each node a point where three or four black lobes spiral out, repeated in a loose lattice. Fine echo lines run along some of the dark bands. Looks like polarised-light stress photography. From a distance: Reads as a pattern of dark swirls and pinwheels on a lighter colour, like twisted fabric or a bent marble pattern; contrast is strong and survives from far away. Measured spec (average): metal 51, roughness 103, coat 108. Shine: satin. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: gt / sports car, open wheel, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Isoclinic Band" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: swirls need big panels to read
Wide quarters and sides show the pinwheel lattice well
High contrast and busy; use numbers on a solid plate or with thick outline.
Thick solid numbers and stripes: bold shapes read over medium-scale swirls
Pairs well with: black, chrome, in whatever colour you give it, silver.
pitfalls: Not tiger or zebra stripes: bands curl into pinwheels and nodes
Not smoke or marble veins: hard pinch points, repeated like a lattice
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers over the busy lobes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 51 (low metal, like carbon or subtle flake), roughness 103 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 108 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, numbers over the busy lobes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: thick solid numbers and stripes: bold shapes read over medium-scale swirls; a plain outline or border band: frames the swirl
Patterns to avoid: other swirl, flow or marble patterns: contours tangle; fine mesh or weave: texture clash
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear: deepens the dark bands; fine sparkle in the light zones only
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
